Cardarion Williams: The first name on the early board belongs to a defender capable of changing an entire protection plan. Williams pairs outstanding pass-rush production with a generational projection, giving Georgia a player whose upcoming season could strengthen his case as the class’s premier prospect.
Malachi Robinson: Robinson gives Ohio State a physical presence who can make offenses pay for testing the middle. The highly regarded safety already brings elite recruiting credentials and strong run support; a standout season in coverage could put a top-three selection firmly within reach.
Willie Mason Jr: Mason can make the distance between the sidelines feel considerably smaller. The former five-star linebacker combines elite coverage ability with exceptional range, giving LSU an answer to offenses that want to isolate defenders in space. He enters the season with top-three potential.
Mwenye Obasanjo: Receivers won’t get an easy release against Obasanjo. Ohio State’s physical corner can match different types of targets, and his partnership with Malachi Robinson gives the Buckeyes a formidable tandem. His versatility should keep him near the top of early draft conversations.
J.T. Rhoads: Rhoads enters the season as the top projected quarterback on the early board, with room to climb even higher. USC’s passer combines a strong arm with impressive accuracy and a knack for finding the end zone, giving his offense an exciting foundation.
Aaron Archuelta: Few areas of the field are out of reach when Archuelta sets his feet. Penn State’s quarterback has elite arm strength, franchise-caliber tools and the athleticism to expand the playbook. His upcoming season offers a chance to turn that physical package into a leading projection.
Cody Ellis: Running behind Ellis can make the right side of an offense a much more inviting place. The former five-star tackle opens lanes with authority and has also spent time at left tackle, giving Penn State an imposing blocker with valuable positional flexibility.
At 6-foot-4, Williams gives Texas a vertical threat who can make smaller defensive backs feel the mismatch. His combination of size and speed carries the potential of a top receiving option, with the upcoming season offering another showcase for his downfield ability.
Nakana'ela Pukahi: Pukahi gives a quarterback an imposing presence on the blind side. Ohio State’s tackle combines elite pass protection with the power to handle physical rushers, placing him among the most secure early top-ten projections as the new college season approaches.
Nick Monk: A routine touch can become a chunk play when Monk has room to operate. Florida State’s dynamic receiver brings the playmaking ability to energize an offense, and his early projection suggests a professional team could eventually build around that explosive potential.
Garrison Fitzwilliam: Quarterbacks can feel a little more comfortable with Fitzwilliam protecting the blind side. Iowa’s tackle handles a variety of pass-rush builds with elite technique, giving him the early profile of a franchise-caliber left tackle and a foundational piece for an offensive line.
J.C. Martens: Martens has already shown Alabama he can thrive in more than one spot. After starting inside at guard, he moved to right tackle and became an outstanding presence, giving teams positional versatility and a strong early case for the first round.
Keshawn White: White brings the kind of athleticism that can change a game off the edge. The former five-star recruit gives LSU a pass rusher with the tools to disrupt an offense and the early projection of a potential difference-maker at the next level.
Kash Bailey: Georgia has more than one edge defender commanding first-round attention. Bailey brings the talent to stand on his own, consistently generating quarterback hits and pressure. His ability to affect the pocket gives the Bulldogs another dangerous presence across the defensive front.
Kevin Alexander Jr: Alexander has the kind of linebacker talent that can change the conversation around a draft class. Clemson’s gifted defender brings the athletic ability to cover ground and make plays, with the potential to climb into the top five as the season unfolds.
Keanu Jones: Jones patrols the deep field like a center fielder tracking a fly ball. Ohio State’s talented safety combines elite zone coverage with reliable tackling, giving the Buckeyes another first-round-caliber defensive back who can cover space and finish when a play reaches him.
ChaCha Oakim: At 6-foot-4, Oakim gives Tennessee a young receiver who can change the shape of a passing attack. His size, speed and hands provide the ingredients for a featured target, and another season offers a chance to show just how high his ceiling can reach.
Johnny Newman: Newman’s 6-foot-6 frame gives Notre Dame a target who can make a quarterback’s job easier downfield. His size and skill suggest the potential to become a featured weapon at the next level, putting him firmly on the early first-round watch list.
Hezekiah Smith: Smith gives Wisconsin a pass rusher who knows how to work a blocker. His technique and consistent career sack production make him a steady threat on the edge, giving an offensive tackle more to prepare for than a single burst off the snap.
Jonathan Brothers: Stanford can put a formidable frame on the edge with Brothers. The big defensive lineman has the size to disrupt an opponent’s running game, giving the front a powerful bookend who can occupy space and make rushing lanes disappear.
A.J. Simms: Simms makes the most of every inch at corner. The Clemson defender pairs elite coverage skills with a productive track record, giving scouts a player who can stay with receivers and affect throws. His play keeps him firmly in the first-round conversation.
Troy Nunez: At 6-foot-2, Nunez brings Notre Dame the length to stay attached to a receiver throughout a route. His coverage ability gives him the potential to make an outside target’s afternoon difficult, putting the corner on the early first-round radar.
Tyler Morgan-Stewart: Morgan-Stewart gives South Carolina a target who can make any throw feel more inviting. The 25-year-old tight end is regarded as having the best hands in the class, regardless of position, and brings the experience to project as an immediate contributor.
Dee Davison: Davison enters the year with momentum after his best season. The former five-star Ole Miss tackle has the physical traits teams look for on the right side, giving him a first-round profile as he builds on the progress already shown.
Taylor Smith-Foster: At 6-foot-5, Smith-Foster brings an imposing frame to the middle of Texas Tech’s defense. His combination of size, skill and physical tools gives scouts an intriguing linebacker to follow, with the potential to make an impact at the professional level.
Jerald Simms-Morrison: Simms-Morrison gives Mississippi State a bigger, athletic option working from the slot. His frame and movement skills create an appealing matchup inside, and his ability to compete for a role early has put him on the first-round watch list.
Decovon Thompson: Thompson brings a rare frame and a nose for the football to Virginia Tech’s secondary. The 6-foot-3 safety has the ball skills to create turnovers, giving a defense an imposing presence on the back end and a player offenses must account for.
Nick Barrientos: Barrientos heads into a new chapter at Miami with the talent that made him a five-star recruit. After beginning his career at Arkansas, the quarterback gets a fresh opportunity to show what he can become and reestablish himself on the early draft board.
Kenneth Bell: There are few players in college football who can run with Bell. The Memphis corner brings elite speed and athletic ability to the secondary, giving him the tools to cover ground quickly and putting him among the most intriguing risers to watch this season.
Narquise Jones: Jones can stretch a defense vertically, then make a defender miss once the ball arrives. The Minnesota receiver combines long speed with open-field ability, giving an offense two ways to create explosive plays and a prospect whose momentum could grow this season.
Kaziri Nyokare: Nyokare has the kind of athletic profile that makes scouts stop and watch. The UConn edge defender is a rare physical specimen with the tools to become a star, and the upcoming season gives him a stage to turn those traits into a bigger impact.
Jeramy McCue: McCue does some of his best work when the running game gets moving. Syracuse’s guard brings the power and movement to create room for backs, giving an offense a physical presence inside and an early first-round candidate for a ground-focused attack.
